_doc: The test registry: ONE list of every automated check, read by tools/run-tests.js (run, select, summarise) and checked by `python3 build.py --check` (every tools/*-smoke.js must be here). Fields: id (the file's name without .js), args, needs (src = straight from src/, dist = the built page, runs a build first; playwright = also needs Chromium, skips itself without), secs (a typical run on one core, for planning), desc (what it proves), covers (regular expressions on a changed file's path from the repo root: `--changed` runs the tests whose covers match), flaky (substrings of FAIL lines that are known random failures: the runner reruns such a test once). Add a test: a row here, nothing else. The numbers of checks are not kept here (they drift): the runner counts the PASS lines.

tests.desc: the world server end to end: join, combat and XP, quests, shop, forge, equip, per-player snapshots, a 2-player boss fight, snapshot size, weather, chat
thousands of garbage messages and mutated saves sent to every handler: nothing may throw, no NaN or negative coins, no non-string items, no prototype pollution

the Shared (claude.ai room) transport's message splitting against a mock 4 KB room: big messages in parts, any order, interleaved, duplicated, lost; ordinary messages with a k field are never taken for parts

the Node host's save stores: a missing account is null, create refuses a second, many saves of one account at once leave one whole record and no temp file (files), and commit in the order asked, a failure not blocking the next, accounts not waiting for each other (Postgres, against a fake pool)
the same garbage as server-fuzz against the deployed setting (testing tools off), and every dev / rwdev message must then change nothing: what a player can really reach
registered accounts: register, log in, tokens, unique names, lock-out, the account's look
elements, the soul, drops, skill upgrades, passives, and all the boss skills cast
elemental reactions: the 15-pair chart, auras, cooldowns, vuln / weak that never stack, guards
the skill-set engine on fixture sets: registry checks, granting, wearing, bonuses, marks, triggers, allies, shields, taunt
the eight shipped skill sets as a cast and what each piece does; the free version-2 testing tools
the power ladder of every set against the best non-set loadout (the damage kits' orderings must hold)

random valid loadout actions by 2 players (unlock sets, wear and take off pieces, passives, class and level changes, fights, saves): the live loadout is valid after every action and after a save, stats stay finite
the character model: slider table, every model's recommended setups, proportions, joints, detail budget, seeded villagers
each signature outfit builds on both bodies at every slider extreme, within its triangle budget, with a weapon dressing for all three classes
the eight look documents in docs/skillkits/looks/ against the built outfits
the main quest, acts I-IV: talks, herbs, kills, grey monsters, lore, old saves and the step migration, professions steps, the bosses
the Hoarfrost Reach: shape, zones, monsters, bosses, the ice wall, quest board and XP for levels 22-30, mining there
the Greyspine: terrain, glacier valley and ice fall, Highmark, zones and monsters, two bosses, water, rock falls
the wandering borders between the four lands and their pins, one land per point, the Greyfall River and its bridge
the continent's coast: sea on the north and east, bays and capes, islets, arenas and doors keep their ground
with the slope limit every village, arena, zone, node and door is still reachable on foot
Glasswell's layout (homes, gates, rim, bridges) and, with Chromium, that its 3D model builds in a real browser within budget
the pendants: items, slot and saves, what each bonus does to a kill and a hit, caps and the level gate
professions, tools and their slots, nodes of every land, gathering and its cast, selling, crafting, brewing, potions
zone tiers I-V: the rules, saves, choosing a tier, the unlock, per-player damage / XP / drops, the creeps above level 60
the XP curve, the soft cap from level 50, saves, the testing tool, a kill never pays for more than 10 levels above you
the eight world bosses' move sets: each fought through three phases; every boss does its own moves and leaves nothing behind
chaos at every world boss (players die, flee, return, disconnect at random): each boss gives up and resets completely, nothing of its fight is left
balance yardstick: a maxed level-60 hero against the level-80 bosses and the ramp below them
the dungeon setup: tiles, layouts of all missions, the baked grid, the four dungeons and bosses, the offer, entrances, reward rules

the Proving Isle (PvP): the island and its bridge, the same numbers for everyone, hits between fighters and not across the water, party spared, no rewards, the knock-out (a shore spot, the gate shut 10 s), no potions, every attack skill fired
parties: invites, /invite, the cap, lead, kick, leave, expiry
dungeon runs on the server: slots, isolation from the world, walls, party health, loot, down / revive / lost, a Purge won

random valid party and dungeon-run actions by 5 players (invite, kick, lead, start a run, leave, revive, die, disconnect, come back): registries stay consistent and nothing is left behind after everyone has gone
the four dungeon bosses fought in a real hall: every move happens and none is shared
the seven mission kits, each won through its boss and lost by its own condition; HUD text, chests, hazards
level-30 dungeon gear, the ring and the soul, Tempering Stones, tempering, the forge's merge rule, saves

flaky: dungeon: the run's monsters have views at the run's level
tests.desc: the built page headless in solo: streaming, monster views, attacking, inventory, skills panel, maps, weather, every boss skill drawn, the Hoarfrost and Greyspine client sides, a dungeon run
the start card (guest, log in, register, errors) and a new account's character editor, against a real server in-process
rebindable keys (defaults, swap, save and load, hints) and hold-Alt

the built Node host as its own process: HTTP (page in brotli/gzip/plain, ETag and 304, lean page, music route and its 404s), raw WebSocket frames (handshake, hello, ping, fragments, garbage, long control frame, flood), SIGTERM saves and exits
accounts on the built server with its real scrypt and file store: register from a guest, unique names, a restart, login by password and by token, wrong passwords and the lock, take-over, logout

the built page (headless, Node's own WebSocket) on the built server as its own process: the host's start card, guest start, roster and snapshots, walking seen by a raw client, chat both ways, Register / Log in through the card, a server that dies under the game

the production save path against a real PostgreSQL (a throwaway cluster, or WILDWOOD_TEST_PG): guest and account rows, scrypt hash, {movedTo}, a restart on the database alone, login by password and token, writes of one account in order; skips (exit 0) without the pg package or PostgreSQL binaries

the built page in phone (LOW) and light (LITE) mode: world loads, lazy far-tile colours, deferred far-village NPCs, solo start, the touch controls (joystick, look drag, jump button), no console errors
the four dungeon doors' client dressing, prompts, maps and sounds
the ring and pendant slots, tempered tiles, the forge's Temper tab, item icons
a dungeon run's client: view, walls, camera, party frame, HUD, results, disposal
the Delve board panel and the join prompt
static check of the two bundles as they run (one scope each): no undefined names, no impossible code (skips itself without ESLint)
docs/MOBS.md and docs/EQUIPMENT.md still match the code (monster, item, balance, drop and boss data; a moved line number only warns)
